item.title: Preserving Order in MongoDB Queries with $in Clause
item.description:
“Preserving Order in MongoDB Queries with $in Clause”

If maintaining the exact order of the input list is critical for your application logic, what strategies are available to impose this desired sequencing on the results?

Forcing Order with MongoDB Aggregation Pipelines

The aggregation framework offers precise control over the output sequence through projection and sorting stages.

Method 1: Assigning Weights via Conditional Logic

This approach involves introducing a calculated field (a “weight”) to each matching document based on its value relative to the input array sequence. Then, a final sort operation uses this weight.

item.title: Oracle SQL Pagination: Efficiently Limit and Offset Query Results
item.description:
“Oracle SQL Pagination: Efficiently Limit and Offset Query Results”

When working with large datasets in Oracle databases, retrieving all records at once can be inefficient. Implementing pagination, which involves fetching data in smaller, manageable chunks, is crucial for performance and user experience. This post delves into various Oracle SQL methods for limiting and offsetting query results, covering both older and newer Oracle versions.

Solution 1: Using Subqueries with ROWNUM

A classic approach for limiting results in older Oracle versions involves nested subqueries and the ROWNUM pseudocolumn.
